requirements.evidence: All contract items are present: migrations create `entities` with `entities_slug_unique` (database/migrations/2026_10_29_000000_create_entities_table.php:16) and `entity_memberships` with cascade FKs, role default employee, `entity_memberships_entity_user_unique` and the generated `owner_seq` + `entity_memberships_one_owner` (database/migrations/2026_10_29_000001_create_entity_memberships_table.php:53-67); models/relations/enum (app/Models/Entity.php:38-55, app/Models/EntityMembership.php:30-67, app/Models/UserRole.php:5-20); both policies cover create/view/update/delete/manageSettings and view/assignRole/delete including owner-immutability and self-removal (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:12-45, app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:10-35); pick stores the session, logs on the audit channel and redirects (app/Http/Controllers/EntitySelectionController.php:17-36); routes match the specified verbs/URLs (routes/web.php:26-29); Dashboard hides the settings URL for non-owners (resources/views/livewire/entity/dashboard.blade.php:15-21); Members implements addMember with `exists:users,email` plus duplicate error on `email`, assignRole restricted to `UserRole::manageable()` with a `role` validation error, owner/last-manager 403s (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:38-119); Settings enforces owner-only mount, non-swappable locked entity id, slug-unique-ignore-self, soft delete + membership delete + session clear, and atomic demote-then-promote transfer with 403 on missing owner/missing admin/self (app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:30-113); required pt_BR/en strings incl. "Transferir propriedade"/"You are the owner of this entity." (lang/pt_BR/ui.php:50-53, lang/en/ui.php:50-53); docs/database-schema.md updated for the one-owner invariant and constraints.

conventions.evidence: Good: migrations have reversible `down()` and named indexes, `#[Fillable]` attribute matches the sibling User model, every Livewire action authorizes server-side via `$this->authorize(...)` (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:42,82,102; app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:48,66,84), docs updated. Deviations: public input properties carry no `#[Validate]`/`rules()` and rules are inlined in each action instead of the project's `#[Validate] + $this->validate()` pattern (`public string $email = '';` app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:27 and :44; `public string $name/$slug/$targetMembershipId` app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:24-28 and :47-56); domain writes (entity update/delete, ownership transfer, membership writes) live in the components rather than `app/Actions/*` as conventions.md requires; `EntitySelectionController` authorizes by hand instead of through a policy (app/Http/Controllers/EntitySelectionController.php:17-20); no CHANGELOG.md `[Unreleased]` entry while docs were updated.

security.evidence: Authorization is enforced on the server in every public action and mount (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:42,82,102; app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:32,48,66,84), action parameters are never trusted: memberships are resolved scoped to the entity (`$entity->memberships()->whereKey($membershipId)->first()` app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:137-141) and the bound entity is `#[Locked]` and re-fetched (app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:15-16,118-121). Input is validated before writes (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:44-47, app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:47-56), all Blade output uses `{{ }}` with no `{!! !!}`, and `$fillable` is deliberate (`#[Fillable(['name','slug'])]` app/Models/Entity.php:14, EntityMembership.php:12). Minor gap only: unused, non-locked server-context properties `public int $entityId` / `public Entity $entity` are serialized to the client (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:23-25, Settings.php:26-28, Dashboard.php:17-18) though nothing reads them, so there is no exploitable path.

tests.evidence: The diff contains no test files at all (no `tests/` path anywhere in change.diff), so none of the new models, policies, migrations, controller, Livewire components or views are covered; conventions.md requires test-first development, unauthorized-call and tamper tests for every Livewire action and a feature test for rendered UI, and the rubric treats 'no tests for new behavior' as 1.

simplicity.evidence: Mostly lean (policies are tiny, transfer is 10 lines, no speculative layers), but there is avoidable duplication: every component carries a third copy of the entity context (`#[Locked] $boundEntityId`, `public int $entityId`, `public Entity $entity` — app/Livewire/Entity/Dashboard.php:15-18, Members.php:21-25, Settings.php:17-28) and the private `entity()` reload helper is repeated verbatim in two components (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:135-138, Settings.php:118-121); lang files add unused duplicate strings `dashboard_welcome` and `entity_owner_notice` (lang/en/ui.php:54,56; lang/pt_BR/ui.php:54,56).

readability.evidence: Small focused methods with clear names and helpful comments (`// Ownership only moves through the explicit transfer flow.` app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:94; the owner_seq comment app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:105-106), consistent with sibling style (typed relations, PHPDoc generics, `#[Layout('layouts::default-page')]`). Docked for dead state: `public int $entityId` is assigned in mount and never used (app/Livewire/Entity/Dashboard.php:17, Members.php:23, Settings.php:27) and `public Entity $entity` is superseded by the re-fetched local (app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:33 vs :36), which also makes the public property and the private `entity()` method easy to confuse.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: models/enum/policies/migrations/factories, the pick controller, three Livewire components and their views, four routes, both lang files, and the requested docs/database-schema.md update. Nothing out-of-scope (no onboarding, switcher, middleware, navbar or billing work) is touched, and no unrelated refactor appears in routes/web.php:26-29 or app/Models/User.php.

issues.explanation: The whole feature ships without a single Pest/PHPUnit test, which breaks the project's test-first rule and the Livewire definition of done (happy path, validation failure, unauthorized call and tamper attempt per action).

Public input properties (`email`, `name`, `slug`, `targetMembershipId`) have no `#[Validate]` attributes or `rules()` method; rules are inlined in each action instead of following the project's documented `#[Validate] + $this->validate()` pattern.

Domain writes (entity update/delete, atomic ownership transfer, membership create/role change/delete) are implemented inside the Livewire components, whereas conventions.md routes domain writes through `app/Actions/*` with authorization inside the action.
docs/database-schema.md was updated as asked, but the change is missing the `[Unreleased]` CHANGELOG entry that the docs-in-sync convention requires.

`public int $entityId` and `public Entity $entity` are server context that Livewire serializes to the browser and are not `#[Locked]`; they are never read, so there is no exploit, but they contradict the 'lock server-only properties' rule and should be removed or locked.
Membership is checked inline (`membershipFor(...) !== null`) instead of through a policy/gate, while conventions.md requires authorization to always go through policies.

The stored generated `owner_seq` column is also declared `->nullable()`; the nullability modifier is redundant (the expression already yields NULL) and generated-column modifiers differ between SQLite and MySQL/MariaDB, so the migration's portability — the point of this column — should be verified on both drivers.
`dashboard_welcome` and `entity_owner_notice` duplicate `entity_welcome`/`owner_notice` and are never referenced, leaving dead translation strings in both locales.

A missing or blank `targetMembershipId` falls into the `whereKey(null)` lookup and returns 403 instead of a validation error on the property, so the transfer form gives no usable feedback (and there is no confirmation step, unlike delete).
Catching any `QueryException` and reporting `ui.member_already_exists` can mislabel unrelated database failures as a duplicate membership.

review.summary: The change implements the entities/memberships data model, enum, policies, pick endpoint, and the three owner-aware Livewire pages with routes, translations and updated schema docs, and the requirements are met including the tricky cases (single owner enforced by a generated column, atomic ownership transfer, no settings link for non-owners). It is functionally solid but ships with no tests at all and misses two project conventions (no `#[Validate]` on public properties, domain writes not in `app/Actions`), so it needs changes before merging.
